We take meaningful action with urgency, but never at the expense of thoughtful consideration. Innovate & Iterate : We embrace challenges and are not afraid to try new things, even if they might fail. With deep understanding and a clear purpose, we can develop creative and bold solutions to tackle challenges. Own the Outcome: We are empowered to take initiative and we maintain transparency in our work and its outcomes. When we execute, we take responsibility for our decisions, measure the success of our innovations, and learn from the results. You'll be responsible for the reliability, performance, and availability of Develocity instances serving paying customers, open-source projects, and public-facing services, plus supporting infrastructure like artifact registries. You'll work on our internally-built Cloud Application Platform, Kubernetes on AWS, and develop deep expertise in it. When incidents happen, you'll troubleshoot issues across the stack, from application to infrastructure. You'll collaborate with the Cloud Platform team to improve the tooling you depend on, and with engineering teams to build reliability into how we ship software. If you like automating things and hate doing the same task twice, you'll fit in well. You'll be part of a distributed, remote-first team that values asynchronous communication and written documentation. Strong self-direction and clear communication across time zones are essential. Responsibilities Operate and maintain all Develocity instances and supporting services. Participate in a follow-the-sun on-call rotation, owning incident response and troubleshooting issues across the stack. Drive automation across application deployment, upgrades, monitoring, self-healing, and recovery. Build and maintain observability for all managed services (logging, metrics, tracing, and alerting). Work with engineering teams to build reliability into features from the start. Run incident response and retrospectives, and make sure we learn from them. Scripting proficiency (Python, Bash) for automation. Experience with 24/7 on-call rotations. Strong written and verbal English communication. Customer-facing incident communication skills. Experience establishing SRE practices in new or growing teams. A culture that values automation over heroics. In-person meetings, such as our annual company offsite and team meetings. Work from home in a remote-first environment. Competitive salaries and equity grants. Location Remote from anywhere in Europe in the GMT timezone. While our team works remotely and is spread across the globe, we deeply value daily interactions and collaboration.

Der technologische Fokus liegt konsequent auf Linux und Open Source . In den kommenden Jahren stehen spannende Themen an: bestehende Anwendungen sollen auf Open Source Alternativen migriert, Cyber Security und Resilience weiter ausgebaut und ein eigener interner Linux basierter KI Server kontinuierlich weiterentwickelt werden. Open Source: Entwickle bestehende Systeme konsequent weiter und begleite Migrationen von Standardsoftware zu geeigneten Open Source Alternativen. Virtualisierung & Automatisierung: Arbeite mit Technologien wie Proxmox, Docker und vSphere und automatisiere Prozesse beispielsweise mit Python und Ansible. Cyber Security: Entwickle Security und Resilience weiter und beschäftige dich mit technischen Anforderungen rund um NIS 2, DSGVO, CRA und TISAX. KI Infrastruktur: Betreue und erweitere den unternehmenseigenen Linux basierten KI-Server und schaffe eine sichere Infrastruktur für die interne Nutzung künstlicher Intelligenz. Technischer Support: Löse komplexere interne IT-Fragestellungen für überwiegend technisch versierte Anwender mit Schwerpunkt auf dem zweiten und dritten Supportlevel. Qualifikation Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker , IT-Systemadministrator, abgeschlossenes Informatikstudium oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation. Mindestens zwei Jahre Berufserfahrung mit klarem Schwerpunkt auf Linux Administration nach Abschluss deiner Ausbildung oder deines Studiums. Sehr gute Linux Kenntnisse: Du arbeitest bereits routiniert mit Linux und möchtest dich nicht erst in das Betriebssystem einarbeiten. Solides Verständnis von Netzwerktechnik, Netzwerkprotokollen und IT-Infrastruktur . Erfahrung mit Virtualisierung oder Containertechnologien wie Proxmox, Docker oder vSphere. Kenntnisse in der Automatisierung , beispielsweise mit Python, Ansible oder vergleichbaren Technologien. Begeisterung für Open Source und Interesse daran, eine IT-Landschaft langfristig auf offenen und sicheren Lösungen aufzubauen. Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens C1 Niveau sowie fließende Englischkenntnisse. Eigenständige, pragmatische Arbeitsweise und Lust darauf, technische Entscheidungen aktiv mitzugestalten und gemeinsam im Team neue Lösungen auszuprobieren. Kenntnisse in Nextcloud, Open Xchange, Nginx, pfSense, OpenVPN, Git oder Ceph sowie Erfahrung mit IT Security sind von Vorteil. Benefits Gestaltungsspielraum: Entscheide aktiv mit, wie sich die interne IT in den Bereichen Linux, Open Source, Cyber Security, Resilience und Automatisierung weiterentwickelt. Spannende Zukunftsprojekte: Arbeite unter anderem an Open Source Migrationen, dem Ausbau der IT Security und einem eigenen internen Linux basierten KI Server. Direkte Zusammenarbeit: Arbeite eng mit der Geschäftsführung zusammen und profitiere von kurzen Entscheidungswegen und viel Freiheit bei technischen Lösungen. Gehalt: Jahresbruttogehalt ab 60.000 € mit Bereitschaft zur deutlichen Überzahlung abhängig von Qualifikation und Erfahrung. Flexibles Arbeiten: Nutze flexible Arbeitszeiten ohne feste Kernarbeitszeit und arbeite in der Regel einen Tag pro Woche im Homeoffice . Individuell kann nach Absprache auch mehr Remote Arbeit möglich sein. 30 Urlaubstage: Profitiere von 30 Tagen Urlaub und individuellen Lösungen, wenn du darüber hinaus einmal eine längere Auszeit benötigst. Weiterentwicklung: Erhalte individuell abgestimmte Weiterbildungen und einen Mentor aus einem anderen Unternehmensbereich als persönlichen Sparringspartner. review_candidates.title: Hardware & Systems Integration Engineer – Cameras, IoT & Sensor Systems
review_candidates.description: About the project We are developing an animal-welfare monitoring platform that combines video, sensor data, human observations and medical records to build individual health and behavioural profiles. Our goal is to help care teams recognise meaningful changes, identify potential welfare concerns earlier and better understand each animal’s individual needs. Development will begin in an operational cat shelter in Greece, using existing cameras and progressively introducing additional sensors and monitoring infrastructure. About the role We are looking for a hands-on Hardware & Systems Integration Engineer to design, install and integrate the physical monitoring infrastructure that will provide data to the platform. Your first priority will be to assess the shelter’s existing camera infrastructure, improve camera positioning and establish reliable access to video. You will then evaluate and integrate additional sensors and connected devices, ensuring that data can be collected consistently and passed reliably to the software and machine-learning systems. This is a practical engineering role requiring both on-site work in Greece for surveys, installation and commissioning and remote development and support. What you’ll work on Camera infrastructure Audit existing cameras, network video recorders, networking, cabling, power and storage. Identify limitations and recommend practical improvements. Determine appropriate camera positions, mounting heights, viewing angles and coverage. Optimise visibility around relevant areas including feeding, drinking, resting and litter stations. Assess blind spots, occlusion, lighting, motion blur and image detail in collaboration with the computer-vision team. Configure IP cameras and network video recorders. Establish reliable access to RTSP/video streams without disrupting existing recording. Sensors & connected devices Evaluate technologies such as weighing scales, RFID/microchip readers, smart feeders, water-monitoring devices, litter sensors, wearables and environmental sensors. Assess data accessibility and practical suitability before equipment is purchased. Integrate devices through APIs, SDKs, messaging protocols or direct hardware interfaces. Develop connectors and integration scripts/services. Work with software engineers to define consistent data structures including timestamps, device identifiers, locations, units and quality indicators. Support association of sensor observations with individual animals while preserving uncertainty where identification is incomplete. Reliability & infrastructure Implement time synchronisation, automatic reconnection and local buffering. Establish device and stream-health monitoring and alerts for missing or interrupted data. Estimate networking, compute, storage and power requirements through practical testing. Coordinate specialist installation or cabling where required. Ensure equipment is secure, maintainable and appropriate for an operational animal-care environment. Maintain equipment inventories, installation maps, configurations and troubleshooting documentation. What we’re looking for Must-have Demonstrated experience deploying and troubleshooting physical monitoring, IP-camera, IoT or comparable connected-device systems in operational environments. Practical experience with camera positioning and image-quality assessment, including field of view, lighting, motion blur, occlusion and day/night operation. Experience configuring IP cameras and network video recorders, including RTSP streams and ONVIF-based integration. Strong networking fundamentals including IP addressing, Ethernet, PoE, switches, bandwidth assessment and secure remote access. Experience integrating at least one type of sensor or connected device through an API, SDK, messaging protocol or direct hardware interface. Ability to write and maintain integration scripts or services. Strong troubleshooting ability across hardware, networking and software. Practical approach to equipment selection, installation, testing and documentation, with attention to cost, maintainability and animal safety. Ability to collaborate effectively with researchers, software developers and non-technical shelter staff. Availability to travel to the shelter in Greece for on-site assessment, installation and commissioning. Nice to have Experience preparing camera systems specifically for computer vision, including camera calibration, overlapping views and consistent capture conditions. Experience designing and developing proprietary hardware products, including embedded systems, PCB design, firmware and electronics. Experience taking hardware from prototype through to production is particularly valuable. Familiarity with FFmpeg, GStreamer or similar video-processing tools. Experience with RFID/microchip readers, load cells, smart feeders, wearables or environmental monitoring. Familiarity with MQTT, Bluetooth Low Energy, Modbus or serial communications. Experience with edge computers, GPU servers, NAS storage, backup systems or UPS equipment. Experience with thermal cameras or audio capture and integration. Basic electronics and prototyping skills. Experience in animal-care, agricultural, scientific/research or similarly demanding field environments. Degree in electrical, electronic, computer or systems engineering, or a related discipline. Initial deliverables Your initial work will include: Infrastructure audit and prioritised improvement plan. Camera and sensor placement map for the pilot. Working video-ingestion setup with stream-health monitoring and recovery. Assessment of priority sensors and initial integration of selected devices. Tested infrastructure specification and equipment budget. Operational handover and troubleshooting documentation.
